target_customer: AI protein design, food, enzyme and therapeutic teams that need high yield production strains; first customer is its sister brand Ten Lives
problem: Computationally designed proteins are hard to make at commercial yield and cost. Terraferma combines ML guided strain engineering with ultra high throughput genetic screens to raise titer.
business_model: Services and licensing: feasibility studies, custom screening, strain licensing or co-development
product_category: Microbial strain engineering platform for protein manufacturing

founders.name: Vicki Mo
education: Columbia University, MS Computer Science (Machine Learning)
previous_startups: Ten Lives (cat food from precision fermentation, co-launched)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: experience fine tuning ML models and shipping digital and physical products; 2015 US and French Division 1 epee fencing national champion. Employers not listed.

founders.name: Ruby Yu
education: Harvard University, BA and PhD in Biological and Biomedical Sciences
previous_startups: Ten Lives (cat food from precision fermentation, co-launched)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: about a decade studying gene expression from yeast to humans, expert on high throughput genetic screens.

competitors.name: Opera Bioscience
competitors.what: Recombinant proteins and growth factors made in a bacterial host for the food industry

technical_complexity.rationale: ML guided strain engineering plus ultra high throughput screens to reach commercial titer is research grade work needing wet lab capability from a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: The site claims more than 10 billion experimental datapoints and proprietary strains, which would compound, but these claims are company stated and a dataset moat is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ginkgo and others offered strain engineering services, but no source seen of an incumbent copying or buying Terraferma through 2026.

market_need_then: AI protein design was producing candidates faster than they could be manufactured, and precision fermentation startups needed higher titer hosts; evidence comes from the company's own pitch and trade coverage, not a quantified source.

branding.domain_note: terraferma.ai, an AI domain rather than .com

identity.visual_style: Technical, numbered steps and italic accents
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical but direct, with data scale claims

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive tagline but similar sounding names (Terra Wave, Terra Oleo, Tierra) appear in search, and no press on the brand was found.

pivots.from: Platform built around one anchor customer, its own Ten Lives cat food brand
pivots.to: Platform serving outside partners in AI protein design, food, enzymes and therapeutics
pivots.why: Company site says that since 2026 it expanded the platform to partners beyond Ten Lives.

outcome_analysis: Terraferma is active with six people and an NSF SBIR award. Its first product proof is Ten Lives cat food, on shelves since 2024, and in 2026 it opened the platform to outside partners. Founders have strong ML and genetics credentials. Funding is small and partly unverified, and commercial traction beyond Ten Lives is not public, so the outcome remains early.
notes: The NSF grant of $275,000 (period began 2025-01-15) is confirmed by HigherGov and referenced on the company site. PitchBook snippets list a seed of $1.66M to $2.16M dated 2022-12-08, a $500K accelerator deal in 2022-09, a $930K grant in 2025-01 and $2.19M total; only seen in a search snippet, unverified and inconsistent with the grant record, so not recorded as rounds. The company site still says it is joining Y Combinator, which looks stale. Employers of the founders not found. Ginkgo Bioworks is named as a service provider only from an undated vendor page, so it is not listed as a dated competitor. The Opera Bioscience entry rests on a search snippet; the article date comes from its URL.
